import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
import shutil

path = '/conf/config.xml'
shutil.copy(path, path + '.bak.pre-publish')

tree = ET.parse(path)
root = tree.getroot()

NODE3 = '10.100.99.12'
NODE1_LAN = '10.100.99.10'
NODE2 = '10.100.99.11'

# --- NAT port-forward (rdr) rule: only for traffic sourced from node3 ---
nat = root.find('nat')
if nat is None:
    nat = ET.SubElement(root, 'nat')

natrule = ET.Element('rule')
ET.SubElement(natrule, 'interface').text = 'lan'
ET.SubElement(natrule, 'ipprotocol').text = 'inet'
ET.SubElement(natrule, 'protocol').text = 'tcp'
src = ET.SubElement(natrule, 'source')
ET.SubElement(src, 'address').text = NODE3
dst = ET.SubElement(natrule, 'destination')
ET.SubElement(dst, 'address').text = NODE1_LAN
ET.SubElement(dst, 'port').text = '80'
ET.SubElement(natrule, 'target').text = NODE2
ET.SubElement(natrule, 'local-port').text = '8080'
ET.SubElement(natrule, 'descr').text = 'antrieb: rdr node1:80 (from node3 only) to node2:8080'
ET.SubElement(natrule, 'associated-rule-id').text = ''
# insert at start of nat rules (after outbound element, order among nat rules mostly irrelevant
# for rdr since it is its own ruleset, but keep it simple by inserting first)
nat.insert(0, natrule)

# --- Filter rules: allow node3, reject everyone else, inserted BEFORE existing rules ---
filt = root.find('filter')
if filt is None:
    filt = ET.SubElement(root, 'filter')

pass_rule = ET.Element('rule')

ET.SubElement(pass_rule, 'protocol').text = 'tcp'

ET.SubElement(reject_rule, 'protocol').text = 'tcp'
